items.title: Cancelling a Shipped order returns 409 with the domain message
items.reason: This is the reported bug: the rule violation from Order.SetCancelledStatus was surfaced as 500. Functional layer because the status code comes from the real endpoint, mediator pipeline and database.

items.title: Cancelling a Paid order returns 409
items.reason: SetCancelledStatus rejects both Paid and Shipped; the Paid branch is a distinct condition that could regress separately.

items.title: Shipping a Cancelled order returns 409
items.reason: The ship endpoint shares the mapping code with cancel; the story says cancel/ship are both mapped to 500 today, so ship needs its own case.

items.title: Shipping an order that is not Paid (Submitted) returns 409
covers: Technical Notes: SetShippedStatus only valid from Paid
items.reason: Ship is only allowed from Paid; a non-terminal, non-Paid status checks the rule is not limited to Cancelled orders.

items.title: Cancelling a nonexistent order returns 404
covers: Suggested fix: 404 when the order does not exist
items.reason: Command returns false for a missing order; the endpoint must tell this apart from a server fault. Functional because it uses the real IOrderQueries lookup.

items.title: Shipping a nonexistent order returns 404
items.reason: Same mapping as cancel but through the ship endpoint; the existing ShipNonExistentOrderFails test asserts 500 and must change.

items.title: Cancelling with order number 0 returns 400 with the validation message
covers: Decisions: validation OrderingDomainException returns 400 with validation messages
items.reason: ValidatorBehavior raises OrderingDomainException wrapping a ValidationException; it must map to 400, not the 409 used for rule violations.

items.title: Shipping with order number 0 returns 400 with the validation message
items.reason: ShipOrderCommandValidator is separate from the cancel validator; the ship path needs its own check of the 400 mapping.

items.title: Empty x-requestid still returns 400 on cancel and ship
items.reason: Regression guard: the story states the empty request id 400 is unchanged by the refactor of the result type. The existing CancelWithEmptyGuidFails and ShipWithEmptyGuidFails tests cover this and must keep passing.

items.title: Cancelling a Submitted order still returns 200
items.reason: Guards that mapping invalid cases did not break the success path of cancel.

items.title: Shipping a Paid order still returns 200
items.reason: Guards the success path of ship after the endpoint rewrite.

items.title: Retrying with the same x-requestid after a 409 is evaluated again
covers: Deviations: transaction and idempotency ClientRequest roll back on a rule violation
items.reason: The deviation makes the ClientRequest row roll back. If it did not, the retry would be treated as a duplicate and return 200, hiding the conflict. This needs real persistence, so functional.

items.title: IdentifiedCommandHandler rethrows OrderingDomainException but still swallows other exceptions
items.reason: The catch filter change is the root of the fix; a unit test with a substituted mediator pins that domain exceptions escape while generic exceptions keep returning the default result.

items.title: A false command result for an existing order stays a 500 problem
items.reason: Ensures the 404 and 409 mappings did not swallow genuine server faults: when the command returns false and the order exists, the endpoint must still return the failure detail with 500.

items.title: POST /api/orders still returns 200 when order creation hits a domain exception
covers: Deviations: CreateOrderAsync catches the propagated exception and keeps previous behavior (200)
items.reason: The handler change must not alter order creation; the story defers fixing that response to BUG-9, so this pins the current behavior against accidental change.
